description: AIIR Unicode evasion test vectors. Each vector contains a homoglyph, invisible character, or Unicode edge case. Conforming implementations MUST produce identical canonical_json, content_hash, and receipt_id for each vector's input_core.

vectors.description: Author name with Cyrillic 'а' (U+0430) instead of Latin 'a' — visually identical, different bytes, different hash
vectors.implementation_notes: Canonical JSON with ensure_ascii=True encodes U+0430 as \u0430. A naive implementation that doesn't escape non-ASCII would produce a different hash.

vectors.description: Subject with Greek 'Α' (U+0391) instead of Latin 'A' — homoglyph in commit subject changes hash
vectors.implementation_notes: After NFKC normalization, U+0391 stays as U+0391 (Greek Alpha). This is a different codepoint than Latin 'A' (U+0041). Detection normalization (TR39 confusable resolution) maps it to 'A' for signal matching, but the canonical JSON preserves the original bytes.

vectors.description: Author name with fullwidth 'Ａ' (U+FF21) instead of ASCII 'A' — NFKC normalizes this to ASCII 'A' but canonical JSON preserves original bytes
vectors.implementation_notes: NFKC normalization converts U+FF21 to U+0041 (ASCII A). But canonical JSON operates on the ORIGINAL string, not the normalized form. Implementations must not NFKC-normalize before hashing.

vectors.description: Author name with Cherokee 'Ꭺ' (U+13AA) instead of Latin 'A' — obscure homoglyph
vectors.implementation_notes: Cherokee A is a less common confusable. Tests that ensure_ascii encoding handles Supplementary Multilingual Plane characters via \uXXXX escaping.

vectors.description: Subject with zero-width joiner (U+200D) between words — invisible but changes hash
vectors.implementation_notes: ZWJ is invisible in most renderers. The canonical JSON encodes it as \u200d. An implementation that strips invisible chars before hashing will get a different hash.

vectors.description: Author name with soft hyphen (U+00AD) — invisible in most fonts, changes hash
vectors.implementation_notes: Soft hyphen is often stripped by display layers but must be preserved in canonical JSON for correct hashing.

vectors.description: Author name with combining grave accent (U+0300) on 'A' — not the precomposed 'À' (U+00C0)
vectors.implementation_notes: NFC normalization would compose A+U+0300 into U+00C0 (À). Canonical JSON must NOT NFC-normalize; it preserves the decomposed form. The hash differs from a receipt that used precomposed À.

vectors.description: Subject with variation selector VS16 (U+FE0F) appended — invisible modifier, changes hash
vectors.implementation_notes: Variation selectors are invisible in plain text contexts but change the byte content. Implementations must preserve them in canonical JSON.
